case_title: State of Rajasthan v. Mehram & Ors.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.27
aggravating_circumstances: Accused were armed with lethal weapons, assault with intention to kill, provocation from the complainant party
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.148, 302, 324/149 IPC, sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Converted conviction under s.302 IPC to s.326 IPC, sentenced to period already undergone
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were involved in a dispute over the use of a field as a passage. On the day of the incident, the accused, armed with weapons, surrounded the victim when he was passing through the fields. The accused struck the victim on the head with a weapon, causing his death. There were beatings from both sides, and the accused fled after the intervention of other villagers. The victim sustained fatal injuries from a single blow to the head, which was intentional. The accused were found to be the aggressors, and the incident escalated into a free fight. The prosecution's case was based on eyewitness accounts and medical evidence, which indicated the accused's intent to kill.
